items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and delivers 400 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?

rubric.why: Identifies the defining efficiency of an ideal system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its efficiency is 100%.

rubric.why: States the relationship between input and useful output in an ideal system.
rubric.description: Its useful output work equals its input work; no energy is lost.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating either relationship.

modelAnswer: In an ideal system, useful output work equals input work; no energy is lost.

items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the equation v² = u² + 2as.

rubric.why: Uses the area under the velocity-time graph to obtain displacement.
rubric.description: The trapezium's area gives s = (u + v)t/2.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the displacement equation obtained from the graph's area.

rubric.why: Uses the graph's slope to express acceleration and time.
rubric.description: The slope gives a = (v − u)/t, so t = (v − u)/a.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the acceleration relation or its rearrangement for time.

rubric.why: Substitutes the time relation into the displacement equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or equivalent intermediate equation.

rubric.why: Reaches the required third equation of motion.
rubric.description: The result simplifies to v² = u² + 2as.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: The displacement is the area under the velocity-time graph.
The area of the trapezium is s = (u + v)t/2.
The slope of the graph gives acceleration: a = (v − u)/t.
Substituting in the displacement equation: s = (u + v)(v − u)/2a.

items.followUp: A room measures 8 m × 5 m × 4 m. If the density of air is 1.2 kg m⁻³, find the mass of air in the room.

rubric.why: Identifies the given density and room dimensions in SI units.
rubric.description: The density is 1.3 kg m⁻³ and the dimensions are 10 m, 7 m and 6 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the given density and all three dimensions.

rubric.why: Selects the volume relation for the rectangular room.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct volume formula.
Award 1 mark for the correct volume with unit.

rubric.why: Uses the relationship between mass, density and volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct mass relation.

rubric.why: Gives the correct mass of air with its unit.
rubric.description: The mass of air is 546 kg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: density = 1.3 kg m⁻³, l = 10 m, b = 7 m, h = 6 m.
Mass of air in the room = 546 kg.

items.followUp: Describe how you would measure the time taken by a pendulum to complete 20 oscillations using a stopwatch.

rubric.why: Describes starting the timing when the event begins.
rubric.description: Press the start button when the event begins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the stopwatch is started at the beginning of the time interval.

rubric.why: Describes stopping the stopwatch and reading the elapsed time.
rubric.description: Press stop when the event ends and read the time shown.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the stopwatch is stopped at the end and its time is read.

modelAnswer: Press the start button when the event whose duration is being measured begins.
Press the stop button when the event ends and read the time shown on the stopwatch.

items.followUp: State whether each quantity is scalar or vector: distance, displacement, speed and velocity.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining feature of a scalar quantity.
rubric.description: A scalar quantity has magnitude only.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a scalar has magnitude only.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining features of a vector quantity.
rubric.description: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a vector has both magnitude and direction.

modelAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only, such as mass or time.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction, such as force or velocity.
